sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在那个黑胶唱片盛行的年代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带上300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年前精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, Senator Dick Durbin spent 16 years trying and failing to pass immigration reform in Congress.
sentences.zh: 今天，参议员迪克·德宾花了16年时间试图在国会通过移民改革，但都以失败告终。

sentences.en: It failed under President Bush.
sentences.zh: 这项改革在布什总统任内失败了。

sentences.en: It failed under President Obama.
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马总统任内也失败了。

sentences.en: Could the outcome of the White House ending DACA be that it passes under President Trump?
sentences.zh: 白宫终止“童年抵美者暂缓遣返”计划（DACA）的结果，会不会反而在特朗普总统任内促成法案通过呢？

sentences.en: It's Thursday, September 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月7日，星期四。

sentences.en: Cheryl Gay-Stolberg, where does the DREAM Act begin in Congress?
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔·盖伊-斯托尔伯格，DREAM法案在国会最初是怎么来的？
zh_words: 谢丽尔·盖伊-斯托尔伯格

sentences.en: The DREAM Act goes all the way back to 2001 when a guidance counselor for a young South Korean woman, a woman whose family immigrated from South Korea,
sentences.zh: DREAM法案可以追溯到2001年，当时一位年轻韩国女性的升学顾问——这位女性的家庭是从韩国移民过来的——

sentences.en: reached out to Senator Dick Durbin of Illinois.
sentences.zh: 联系了伊利诺伊州的参议员迪克·德宾。

sentences.en: A young woman named Teresa, Teresa Lee, in Chicago, came to this country undocumented at the age of two.
sentences.zh: 那是一个名叫特蕾莎·李的年轻女孩，她两岁时就以无证身份来到了芝加哥。

sentences.en: Senator Durbin spoke to The Times the day DACA was rescinded.
sentences.zh: DACA被废除的那天，德宾参议员接受了《纽约时报》的采访。

sentences.en: She was in a very poor family, but she learned how to play the piano and turned out to be a prodigy.
sentences.zh: 她出身贫寒，但学会了弹钢琴，而且展现出了惊人的天赋。

sentences.en: By the time she was finishing high school, she was being encouraged to apply to Juilliard and the Manhattan Conservatory of Music.
sentences.zh: 高中快毕业时，她被鼓励申请茱莉亚音乐学院和曼哈顿音乐学院。

sentences.en: And so when she sat down to do the application, said to her mother, what do I put here for nationality or citizenship?
sentences.zh: 当她坐下来填写申请表时，问母亲：“国籍或公民身份这一栏我该填什么？”

sentences.en: Her mother said, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 她母亲说：“我不知道。”

sentences.en: So they contacted us and said, what can we do?
sentences.zh: 于是他们联系了我们，问我们能做些什么。

sentences.en: Well, it turned out the law was very clear and very cruel.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，当时的法律既明确又残酷。

sentences.en: It said that Teresa Lee had to leave the United States for 10 years and then petitioned to come back in.
sentences.zh: 法律规定特蕾莎·李必须离开美国10年，然后才能申请重新入境。

sentences.en: I thought for a girl who was probably 18 at the time, that was a pretty harsh outcome.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于一个当时大概才18岁的女孩来说，这个结果太严苛了。

sentences.en: And this touched Dick Durbin, or so he says, and he introduced the DREAM Act as a result.
sentences.zh: 这件事触动了迪克·德宾，至少他是这么说的，于是他提出了DREAM法案。

sentences.en: Footnote on Teresa.
sentences.zh: 关于特蕾莎的后续：

sentences.en: Went to the Manhattan Conservatory of Music, graduated, played in Carnegie Hall, stayed on in New York, married a jazz musician, became legal, mother of two.
sentences.zh: 她去了曼哈顿音乐学院，毕业后在卡内基音乐厅演出，留在了纽约，嫁给了一位爵士乐手，获得了合法身份，还是两个孩子的母亲。

sentences.en: Now I believe she's completed her Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 现在我相信她已经拿到了音乐博士学位。

sentences.en: in music.
sentences.zh: 在音乐领域。

sentences.en: But we introduced the bill, and it was interesting what happened next.
sentences.zh: 但我们提出了这项法案，接下来发生的事情很有意思。

sentences.en: The Republicans supported it.
sentences.zh: 共和党人支持它。

sentences.en: Orrin Hatch was my original co-sponsor of the bill.
sentences.zh: 奥林·哈奇是我最初的法案共同提案人。

sentences.en: With regard to the DREAM Act, a lot of these kids are brought in as infants.
sentences.zh: 关于DREAM法案，这些孩子很多都是婴儿时期被带过来的。

sentences.en: They don't even know that they're not citizens until they graduate from high school.
sentences.zh: 他们直到高中毕业都不知道自己不是公民。

sentences.en: And if they've lived good lives and they've done good things, why would we penalize them and not let them at least go to school?
sentences.zh: 如果他们一直循规蹈矩，做了很多好事，我们为什么要惩罚他们，连让他们上学的机会都不给呢？

sentences.en: Cheryl, I find it really striking that Senator Durbin co-sponsored this legislation protecting young undocumented immigrants with Orrin Hatch,
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，我觉得很引人注目的一点是，德宾参议员竟然与奥林·哈奇共同发起了这项保护年轻无证移民的立法，

sentences.en: who's the Republican senator from Utah.
sentences.zh: 他可是来自犹他州的共和党参议员。

sentences.en: He is a Republican co-sponsoring this legislation.
sentences.zh: 他是一位共和党人，却共同发起了这项立法。

sentences.en: So what does that tell us about that moment?
sentences.zh: 那么这说明了当时的情况如何？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's really interesting, too, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我觉得这确实非常有趣。

sentences.en: And you have to think back in 2001.
sentences.zh: 你得回想一下2001年的时候。

sentences.en: I think compassion is a noble calling.
sentences.zh: 我认为同情心是一种高尚的召唤。

sentences.en: George W.
sentences.zh: 乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush had just been elected president, just taken over in the White House.
sentences.zh: 布什刚刚当选总统，刚刚接管白宫。

sentences.en: And it's on this ground that I will take my political stand.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个立场上，我将表明我的政治态度。

sentences.en: He was from Texas.
sentences.zh: 他来自德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: El sueño americano es para ti.
sentences.zh: 美国梦是属于你的。

sentences.en: He was very sympathetic to Hispanics.
sentences.zh: 他对拉美裔非常同情。

sentences.en: He won 40 percent of the Hispanic vote.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了40%的拉美裔选票。

sentences.en: And he was talking about an immigration overhaul.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在谈论移民改革。

sentences.en: We must remember that the vast majority of illegal immigrants are decent people who work hard.
sentences.zh: 我们必须记住，绝大多数非法移民都是努力工作的正派人。

sentences.en: And I don't think that the issue was as nearly as toxic for Republicans as it later became.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为当时这个问题对共和党人来说像后来那样具有毒性。

sentences.en: And that every human being has dignity and value, no matter what their citizenship papers say.
sentences.zh: 每个人都拥有尊严和价值，无论他们的公民身份文件上写着什么。

sentences.en: Durbin, you know, introduces the bill in 2001.
sentences.zh: 德宾在2001年提出了这项法案，你知道的。

sentences.en: And there's a fair amount of support for it among Republicans at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时共和党人对它有相当多的支持。

sentences.en: But it kind of languishes around and doesn't really go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但它后来就一直搁置，没能取得什么进展。

sentences.en: Fast forward several attempts to move the bill without success.
sentences.zh: 快进到后来几次试图推动该法案但均未成功。

sentences.en: Along comes a new senator named Barack Obama as my colleague.
sentences.zh: 后来出现了一位新参议员，名叫巴拉克·奥巴马，他是我的同事。

sentences.en: He co-sponsors it with me.
sentences.zh: 他和我共同发起了这项法案。

sentences.en: We then get into comprehensive immigration reform.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始进行全面的移民改革。

sentences.en: And by 2006, when it's included in a comprehensive immigration reform bill, the politics have totally changed.
sentences.zh: 到了2006年，当它被纳入全面移民改革法案时，政治环境已经完全变了。

sentences.en: We cannot make it easy on those who have chosen to be illegally here, to disobey our laws.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让那些选择非法留在这里、违抗我们法律的人变得轻松。

sentences.en: So we're starting to see at that time sort of the nascent beginnings of the Tea Party movement, which really takes off, you know, around the summer of 2009.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时开始看到茶党运动的萌芽，它在2009年夏天左右真正兴起，你知道的。

sentences.en: Everybody and their mama are trying to come here.
sentences.zh: 每个人和他们的妈妈都想来这里。

sentences.en: We've got to protect our freedom.
sentences.zh: 我们必须保护我们的自由。

sentences.en: And the Tea Party movement is very strongly anti-immigration.
sentences.zh: 而茶党运动是非常强烈的反移民运动。

sentences.en: The time has passed to lobby or request these elected or appointed officials to honor their oath of office and our laws.
sentences.zh: 现在已经过了游说或请求这些民选或任命的官员履行其就职誓言和遵守我们法律的时候了。

sentences.en: We now have to demand that those in office who aid and abet illegal aliens be removed from office and prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 我们现在必须要求那些协助和教唆非法外籍人士的在职官员被免职并受到起诉。

sentences.en: By the end of the 2000s, this DREAM Act is really toxic for Republicans who are terrified that they will get primary challenges from the right,
sentences.zh: 到了2000年代末，DREAM法案对共和党人来说真的成了毒药，他们非常担心会受到来自右翼的初选挑战，

sentences.en: from Tea Party candidates who will knock them out of office.
sentences.zh: 来自那些会把他们踢出局的茶党候选人。

sentences.en: And it seems like a vote for the DREAM Act would be potentially for these Republicans just a ticket out of their own jobs.
sentences.zh: 看起来，投票支持DREAM法案对这些共和党人来说，可能就是丢掉饭碗的入场券。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And one of those Republicans is Orrin Hatch, the original co-sponsor of the DREAM Act with Durbin in 2001.
sentences.zh: 而其中一位共和党人就是奥林·哈奇，他曾是2001年与德宾共同发起DREAM法案的人。

sentences.en: He skipped a vote on it in 2010, but says he would have voted against it.
sentences.zh: 他在2010年跳过了投票，但表示如果投的话他会投反对票。

sentences.en: ...pandering to the Hispanics in this country and others by pretending that they're going to do something about immigration.
sentences.zh: ……通过假装他们要解决移民问题来迎合这个国家的拉美裔和其他人。

sentences.en: And you know doggone well, there's no way they can put an immigration bill through.
sentences.zh: 你心里很清楚，他们根本不可能通过移民法案。

sentences.en: So, Cheryl, is that sort of the end of whatever hope this bill had in Congress?
sentences.zh: 所以，谢丽尔，这是否意味着该法案在国会的希望彻底破灭了？

sentences.en: It feels like a pretty meaningful symbol when the co-sponsor of the original bill turns away from it in fear of losing his seat.
sentences.zh: 当最初法案的共同提案人因为害怕丢掉席位而背弃它时，这感觉是一个非常有意义的象征。

sentences.en: Well, interestingly, Michael, in 2010, the bill actually passed the House but did not get through the Senate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有趣的是，迈克尔，2010年该法案实际上在众议院通过了，但没能在参议院通过。

sentences.en: And then, by 2013,
sentences.zh: 然后，到了2013年，

sentences.en: language allowing DREAMers to stay in this country and work or attend school is included in a broader immigration package that actually does pass the Senate with 68 votes.
sentences.zh: 允许“追梦人”留在这个国家工作或上学的条款被纳入了一项更广泛的移民方案中，该方案确实以68票在参议院获得通过。

sentences.en: But the bill failed in the House.
sentences.zh: 但该法案在众议院失败了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Passes one, fails the other.
sentences.zh: 通过了一个，另一个失败了。

sentences.en: Passes the other, fails the other.
sentences.zh: 通过了另一个，前一个又失败了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And never at the right time.
sentences.zh: 而且从来没有在正确的时间。

sentences.en: One of the first things you learn in the Senate is you'd better be patient, because most of the important things you want to do take a long time.
sentences.zh: 在参议院学到的第一件事就是你最好有耐心，因为大多数你想做的重要事情都需要很长时间。

sentences.en: I had no idea when I introduced this bill 15 or 16 years ago we'd still be talking about it today.
sentences.zh: 15或16年前我提出这项法案时，根本没想到今天我们还在谈论它。

sentences.en: We've had our ups and downs.
sentences.zh: 我们经历过起起落落。

sentences.en: We've won a few votes in the Senate, lost a few.
sentences.zh: 我们在参议院赢过几次投票，也输过几次。

sentences.en: The House has won a few.
sentences.zh: 众议院也赢过几次。

sentences.en: But we've never been able to put it together in one year.
sentences.zh: 但我们从来没能让它在同一年里两院都通过。

sentences.en: Obama goes on to be elected president, and we're not passing the DREAM Act.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马后来当选总统，我们还是没能通过DREAM法案。

sentences.en: We send a letter in 2010 saying to the president, can you do something with your presidential power to protect these young people?
sentences.zh: 我们在2010年给总统写了一封信，问他能不能利用总统权力保护这些年轻人？

sentences.en: We don't get a response.
sentences.zh: 我们没有得到回应。

sentences.en: Time passes.
sentences.zh: 时间流逝。

sentences.en: The next year, we send a letter, 23 senators to President Obama saying, can you do something to help these young people?
sentences.zh: 第二年，我们23位参议员又写信给奥巴马总统，问他能不能做点什么来帮助这些年轻人？

sentences.en: And DACA emerges as their approach to this.
sentences.zh: 于是DACA作为他们解决这个问题的方法出现了。

sentences.en: So Obama, you know, finally gets fed up, and he decides Congress isn't going to act, so he's going to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以奥巴马终于受够了，他决定既然国会不采取行动，那他就要自己动手。

sentences.en: But he makes clear that he himself wants Congress to act, that he's just doing this because Congress won't.
sentences.zh: 但他明确表示，他本人希望国会采取行动，他这么做只是因为国会不作为。

sentences.en: And he issues a call to lawmakers to take care of this problem.
sentences.zh: 他向立法者发出呼吁，要求他们解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And I've said time and time and time again to Congress that send me the DREAM Act, put it on my desk, and I will sign it right away.
sentences.zh: 我一次又一次地对国会说，把DREAM法案送到我桌上，我会立刻签署。

sentences.en: So, Cheryl, what happens to the DREAM Act in Congress after President Obama essentially circumvents Congress and issues this executive action?
sentences.zh: 那么，谢丽尔，在奥巴马总统实际上绕过国会并采取这一行政行动后，DREAM法案在国会发生了什么？

sentences.en: His idea is that it would galvanize Congress to do something on this.
sentences.zh: 他的想法是这会激励国会在这个问题上有所作为。

sentences.en: Did that actually happen?
sentences.zh: 这真的发生了吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Oh, so Congress moves on to other things.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以国会转向了其他事情。

sentences.en: It didn't really galvanize Congress to act because lawmakers figured, well, that problem is taken care of.
sentences.zh: 它并没有真正激励国会采取行动，因为立法者们认为，好吧，那个问题已经解决了。

sentences.en: So we might as well just move on to something else.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不如去做点别的。

sentences.en: Now it's time for America to bind the wounds of division.
sentences.zh: 现在是美国治愈分裂创伤的时候了。

sentences.en: We have to get together.
sentences.zh: 我们必须团结起来。

sentences.en: To all Republicans and Democrats and independents across this nation, I say it is time for us to come together as one united people.
sentences.zh: 我对全国所有的共和党人、民主党人和独立人士说，现在是我们作为一个统一的民族团结起来的时候了。

sentences.en: It's time.
sentences.zh: 是时候了。

sentences.en: I pledge to every citizen of our land that I will be president for all Americans.
sentences.zh: 我向我们土地上的每一位公民承诺，我将成为所有美国人的总统。

sentences.en: And this is so important to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我很重要。

sentences.en: So now we have a new president.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了一位新总统。

sentences.en: He's elected in November.
sentences.zh: 他在11月当选。

sentences.en: I call President Obama and say, what are we going to do about these DACA-protected young people and DREAMers?
sentences.zh: 我打电话给奥巴马总统说，我们该如何处理这些受DACA保护的年轻人和“追梦人”？

sentences.en: And he said, I'm going to bring it up with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会向特朗普总统提出这个问题。

sentences.en: I'll talk to him, President-elect Trump at the time.
sentences.zh: 我会和他谈谈，当时还是候任总统的特朗普。

sentences.en: So the story goes,
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，

sentences.en: President Obama told me later that what was scheduled to be a 30-minute meeting turned out to be 90 minutes in the White House Oval Office between President-elect Trump and President Obama.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统后来告诉我，原定30分钟的会议，结果在白宫椭圆形办公室里，候任总统特朗普和奥巴马总统谈了90分钟。

sentences.en: And a large part of it was about this.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分内容就是关于这个问题的。

sentences.en: What's he going to do with DACA and the DREAMers?
sentences.zh: 他打算怎么处理DACA和“追梦人”？

sentences.en: The president is trying to tell him that, you know, fairness and justice suggest we've got to protect them.
sentences.zh: 总统试图告诉他，公平和正义要求我们必须保护他们。

sentences.en: And secondly, strictly politically from a PR viewpoint, hurting these young people is not going to be popular.
sentences.zh: 其次，纯粹从政治和公关角度来看，伤害这些年轻人并不会受欢迎。

sentences.en: And the president felt like he was getting through to President-elect Trump on the subject.
sentences.zh: 总统觉得他在这个问题上说服了候任总统特朗普。

sentences.en: Well, lo and behold, it turns out that President Trump starts changing his campaign rhetoric on the issue.
sentences.zh: 嗯，结果出人意料，特朗普总统开始改变他在这个问题上的竞选言论。

sentences.en: He's more understanding and friendlier to these young people.
sentences.zh: 他对这些年轻人更加理解，也更友好了。

sentences.en: I meet Donald Trump for the first time on his inauguration day.
sentences.zh: 我在就职典礼那天第一次见到唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I said, thank you for the nice things you're saying about the DREAMers and DACA.
sentences.zh: 我说，谢谢你对“追梦人”和DACA说了那么多好话。

sentences.en: And I said, I want to work with you on that.
sentences.zh: 我说，我想在这方面与你合作。

sentences.en: And he looks at me and he says, don't worry about those kids.
sentences.zh: 他看着我说，别担心那些孩子。

sentences.en: We're going to take care of the DREAMers.
sentences.zh: 我们会照顾好“追梦人”的。

sentences.en: And I take him to his word.
sentences.zh: 我信守他的承诺。

sentences.en: And I meant it.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: I've had four or five personal meetings with Jared Kushner and Lindsey Graham talking about this issue.
sentences.zh: 我和贾里德·库什纳以及林赛·格雷厄姆就这个问题进行了四五次私人会谈。

sentences.en: So that is the prelude leading up to today.
sentences.zh: 这就是通往今天的前奏。

sentences.en: We have many important priorities in September, really critical priorities in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我们在九月份有很多重要的优先事项，在参议院确实有非常关键的优先事项。

sentences.en: This is one of them.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Now's the time.
sentences.zh: 现在是时候了。

sentences.en: Don't wait six months.
sentences.zh: 不要再等六个月了。

sentences.en: Do it now.
sentences.zh: 现在就做。

sentences.en: You never know what's going to be on the Senate agenda a month from now.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道一个月后参议院的议程上会有什么。

sentences.en: You don't know what's going to happen next month in North Korea.
sentences.zh: 你不知道下个月朝鲜会发生什么。

sentences.en: You know what's going to happen next month in Florida.
sentences.zh: 你知道下个月佛罗里达会发生什么。

sentences.en: You have no idea what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: I've been around here long enough.
sentences.zh: 我在这里待的时间够长了。

sentences.en: You need to seize the moment.
sentences.zh: 你需要抓住时机。

sentences.en: September is the moment.
sentences.zh: 九月是关键时刻。

sentences.en: So then we get to now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在谈到了当下。

sentences.en: And the Trump White House explicitly demands that Congress solve this problem.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普白宫明确要求国会解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Where are we actually at in Congress?
sentences.zh: 国会目前进展如何？

sentences.en: You're literally inside Congress right now as this issue gets to them.
sentences.zh: 当这个问题摆在国会面前时，你正身处其中。

sentences.en: It's almost mind-blowing to me, Michael, the way the politics around this have shifted.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，围绕这个问题的政治风向转变之大，让我感到不可思议。

sentences.en: You've got the Speaker of the House saying this problem needs to be addressed.
sentences.zh: 众议院议长已经表示需要解决这个问题。

sentences.en: You've got Lindsey Graham, the senator from South Carolina, conservative, pairing up now with Dick Durbin.
sentences.zh: 来自南卡罗来纳州的保守派参议员林赛·格雷厄姆，现在也开始与迪克·德宾联手了。

sentences.en: Let's put it this way.
sentences.zh: 我们可以这样说。

sentences.en: If I were a Democrat, I would want Dick Durbin at the table.
sentences.zh: 如果我是民主党人，我会希望迪克·德宾参与谈判。

sentences.en: He is the father, grandfather, and soon-to-be great-grandfather of the Dream Act.
sentences.zh: 他是《梦想法案》之父、祖父，很快就要成为曾祖父了。

sentences.en: I have never seen a man so committed to a cause as Dick has been committed to fixing this problem for the Dream Act kids.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过像迪克这样致力于解决“梦想生”问题的人。

sentences.en: There is no way he'll be dealt out.
sentences.zh: 他绝不可能被排除在外。

sentences.en: I want to be there, too, because I've got to know a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 我也想参与其中，因为我认识他们当中的许多人。

sentences.en: And actually, I want to celebrate with Senator Durbin an accomplishment for the nation, which is to take care of these kids.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想和德宾参议员一起庆祝为国家取得的一项成就，那就是照顾好这些孩子。

sentences.en: One more question.
sentences.zh: 再问一个问题。

sentences.en: And I think this is kind of a lesson.
sentences.zh: 我认为这算是一个教训。

sentences.en: In a way, it reminds me of the lesson of health care, which is that once you give something to people, it's really hard to take it away.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这让我想起了医疗保健带来的教训，即一旦你给予人们某种东西，就很难再收回。

sentences.en: And Congress has been not willing to do this for 16 years.
sentences.zh: 国会已经有16年不愿处理这件事了。

sentences.en: But suddenly, when confronted with the prospect of all of these Dreamers, young people who are working, some who are in medical school, they're serving in the military,
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，当面对所有这些“梦想生”的前景时——那些正在工作、有的在读医学院、有的在服兵役的年轻人，

sentences.en: they're saving people's lives in Houston during Hurricane Harvey, confronted with those kinds of stories, they are unwilling simply to walk away.
sentences.zh: 那些在哈维飓风期间在休斯顿拯救他人生命的年轻人，面对这些故事，他们无法简单地置之不理。

sentences.en: So where does that leave us?
sentences.zh: 那么这让我们处于什么境地？

sentences.en: Is it possible that the Congress, which couldn't get this passed under a Democratic president, will now do it under a Republican president who seems very anti-immigration reform?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能，在民主党总统任内无法通过的国会，现在会在一位看起来非常反移民改革的共和党总统任内通过它？

sentences.en: It's possible, but it's not certain yet.
sentences.zh: 有可能，但还不能确定。

sentences.en: And I say that because it's clear to me that Republicans, the hardliners on immigration, will want something extracted for passage of this.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为我很清楚，共和党内那些在移民问题上的强硬派，会要求在通过此法案时获得一些交换条件。

sentences.en: In return, right?
sentences.zh: 作为回报，对吧？

sentences.en: In return.
sentences.zh: 作为回报。

sentences.en: They will want more money for border security, funding for a border wall.
sentences.zh: 他们会要求更多的边境安全资金，以及边境墙的拨款。

sentences.en: We heard Lindsey Graham say he thinks that there could be a marriage between the Dream Act and border security funding.
sentences.zh: 我们听到林赛·格雷厄姆说，他认为《梦想法案》和边境安全拨款之间可以达成某种结合。

sentences.en: We had Democrats, a very strong song of Democrats today on Capitol Hill, calling for a quick up or down vote on the Dream Act alone.
sentences.zh: 今天在国会山上，民主党人发出了非常强烈的呼声，要求对《梦想法案》进行单独的快速投票。

sentences.en: Chuck Schumer, the Democratic leader of the Senate, said that if House and Senate leadership won't put the Dream Act on its own on the floor for a vote in September.
sentences.zh: 参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默表示，如果众议院和参议院领导层不在九月份将《梦想法案》单独提交表决。

sentences.en: If a Clean Dream Act does not come to the floor in September, we're prepared to attach it to other items this fall until it passes.
sentences.zh: 如果九月份不能提交一份纯粹的《梦想法案》，我们准备在今年秋天将其附加到其他议案上，直到它通过为止。

sentences.en: So while there seems to be broad bipartisan agreement that the Dreamers should be allowed to stay here in some form, the devil, as always, is going to be in the details.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然两党似乎达成了一种广泛共识，即应该允许“梦想生”以某种形式留在这里，但魔鬼总是在细节之中。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to see a lot of negotiation and back and forth.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将看到大量的谈判和反复博弈。

sentences.en: And it's sort of too soon to tell how that exactly is going to play out.
sentences.zh: 现在断言事情会如何发展还为时过早。

sentences.en: So, Cheryl, the case could theoretically be made that President Trump, who, of course, campaigned on a platform of cracking down on immigration in a major way,
sentences.zh: 那么，谢丽尔，理论上可以这样说：特朗普总统——他当然是以严厉打击移民为竞选纲领的——

sentences.en: in throwing this issue back to Congress, could ultimately accomplish something that Congress itself failed to do for 16 years.
sentences.zh: 通过将这个问题抛回给国会，最终可能会完成国会自身16年来未能完成的事情。

sentences.en: Including under Democratic President Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 包括在民主党总统巴拉克·奥巴马任内。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That would be something.
sentences.zh: 那将是一件了不起的事。

sentences.en: It would be, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 确实会是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Cheryl, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: As always, Michael.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Senator Durbin spoke with my colleague, Yamiche Alcindor, who's been reporting this story with Cheryl Stolbert.
sentences.zh: 德宾参议员接受了我的同事亚米切·阿尔辛多的采访，她一直与谢丽尔·斯托尔伯特共同报道这个故事。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com免费直播部分采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Hurricane Irma, one of the most powerful Atlantic storms ever recorded, is forecast to hit Florida by Sunday, potentially causing catastrophic flooding.
sentences.zh: 飓风“艾尔玛”是有记录以来最强大的大西洋风暴之一，预计将于周日袭击佛罗里达州，可能造成灾难性的洪水。

sentences.en: The Category 5 storm first made landfall in the Caribbean early Wednesday morning, battering the islands as it headed on toward Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 这场五级风暴于周三清晨首次在加勒比海登陆，在前往波多黎各的途中重创了沿途岛屿。

sentences.en: We essentially came to a deal, and I think the deal will be very good.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上达成了一项协议，我认为这项协议会非常好。

sentences.en: We had a very, very cordial and professional meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一次非常、非常亲切且专业的会谈。

sentences.en: In a surprise decision during a meeting at the White House on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 在周三白宫举行的一次会议上，出现了一个令人惊讶的决定，

sentences.en: President Trump struck a three-month budget deal with Democratic congressional leaders to increase the federal debt limit and finance the government through mid-December.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统与民主党国会领袖达成了一项为期三个月的预算协议，以提高联邦债务上限并为政府提供资金至12月中旬。

sentences.en: The plan combines the debt ceiling increase with billions of dollars in emergency relief aid for Hurricane Harvey.
sentences.zh: 该计划将提高债务上限与数十亿美元的哈维飓风紧急救援资金结合在了一起。

sentences.en: In going with the Democrats' plan, the president undercut Republicans like House Speaker Paul Ryan
sentences.zh: 通过采纳民主党的计划，总统削弱了众议院议长保罗·瑞安等共和党人，

sentences.en: and Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, who had come to the White House with their own proposal and rejected the Democrats' proposal just hours earlier.
sentences.zh: 以及参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔的立场，他们此前带着自己的提案来到白宫，并在几个小时前刚刚拒绝了民主党的提议。

sentences.en: Look, the president can speak for himself, but his feeling was that we needed to come together to not create a picture of divisiveness at a time of genuine national crisis.
sentences.zh: 听着，总统可以为自己代言，但他的感觉是，在真正的国家危机时刻，我们需要团结一致，而不是制造分裂的形象。

sentences.en: And that was the rationale, I'm confident.
sentences.zh: 我相信这就是他的理由。

sentences.en: President Trump then took it a step further on Wednesday, talking to reporters on board Air Force One about Congress's effort to legalize the DREAM Act.
sentences.zh: 周三，特朗普总统更进一步，在“空军一号”上向记者谈到了国会为《梦想法案》合法化所做的努力。

sentences.en: We had a very good meeting with Nancy Pelosi and Chuck Schumer.
sentences.zh: 我们与南希·佩洛西和查克·舒默进行了一次非常好的会谈。

sentences.en: Neglecting to mention that Speaker Ryan and Senator McConnell had also been there.
sentences.zh: 却忽略了提到瑞安议长和麦康奈尔参议员当时也在场。

sentences.en: And Chuck and Nancy would like to see something happen, and so do I.
sentences.zh: 查克和南希希望能看到事情有所进展，我也是。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们要为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean, do they black out to go to sleep?
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是睡着了就“断片”了。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》即可收听。
